MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  LA VERNE HELD IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  OF THE LA VERNE CITY HALL
  Monday, March 4, 2019

1.  A regular meeting of the La Verne City Council was called to order by Mayor Kendrick at 6: 30 p. m.

2  Council Members present:  Mayor Don Kendrick
  Mayor Pro Tern Muir Davis
  Council Member Robin Carder
  Council Member Charlie Rosales
  Council Member Tim Hepburn

  Absent:  None.

  Advisory personnel present:  City Manager Robert Russi
  City Attorney Robert L. Kress
  Assistant City Manager/ Public Works Director Dan Keesey
  Assistant City Clerk Lupe Gaeta Estrella
  Community Development Director Eric Scherer
  Community Services Director Bill Aguirre
  Police Chief Nick Paz
  Police Captain Colleen Flores
  Finance Manager Nathan Statham
  Deputy Public Works Director Anthony Ciotti
  Senior Planner Candice Bowcock
  Personnel Officer JR Ranells

3.  Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Kendrick.

4,  Badge  Pinning Ceremony for  Mayor Kendrick, on behalf of the City Council, congratulated Daniel Carrasco
  Corporal Daniel Carrasco  for his promotion to Corporal. He reported that Daniel was born in the City of
  Glendora and graduated from Glendora High School in 2006. He studied
  Criminal Justice in college and began his law enforcement career with the
  La Verne Police Department in 2009, as a Reserve Police Officer and a
  Parking Enforcement Officer. In 2013, Daniel completed the Los Angeles
  County Sheriff' s Academy and was hired as a Los Angeles County Sheriff' s
  Deputy. During Daniel' s time as a Deputy Sheriff, he was assigned to the
  Men' s Central Jail in Los Angeles. In 2015, he was hired as a La Verne Police
  Officer. He is currently assigned to the patrol division and is a certified Field
  Training Officer. In 2016, 2017, and 2018, Daniel was the recipient of the
  10851 pin award that recognizes Police Officers for their outstanding
  achievement in detection, investigation, and apprehension of automobile
  thieves. His mother, Diane Heinig pinned his badge.

  De Novo Planning Group  Amanda Tropiano, De Novo Planning Group provided the current status of the
  General Plan Update with a slide presentation.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, March 4, 2019, Page 2

5.  Consent Calendar  It was moved by Hepburn, seconded by Carder, and unanimously carried to
  accept, approve, or act on the Consent Calendar items, except for the Item No.
  5a, City Council Minutes of January 22, 2019, were pulled for correction and
  Item No. 5c, Treasurer Report was pulled for correction.

  City Council Minutes  City Council Minutes of January 22, 2019, not approved. Pulled from the
  Consent Calendar for correction.

  Registers of Audited Demands  Register of Audited Demands as follows:

  February 13, 2019, in the amount of$ 737, 228. 25
  February 20, 2019, In the amount of$ 503, 536. 13

  Staff recommended approval of the Register of Audited Demands. Approved
  as recommended.

  Treasurer' s Report  Treasurer' s Report for the Month of January 31, 2019. Pulled to reflect
  correct year of 2019 not 2018 and staff to make change. Approved.

  Tentative Settlement Reached  Mayor Kendrick stated that a tentative settlement was reached with La Verne
  with  La Verne Firefighters on  Firefighters on both the State and Federal Lawsuits. He stated that the City of
  Both the State and Federal  La Verne' s municipal self- insurance carrier, California JPIA, agreed to a
  Lawsuits  tentative settlement with the La Verne Firefighters Association in order to
  resolve both pending state and federal lawsuits. Those involved in the decision
  believe this type of resolution will prevent prolonged and expensive
  proceedings and allow the City to move forward and begin rebuilding bridges
  with La Verne Fire Department employees. While the City looked forward to
  our day in court, we ultimately agreed with the CJPIA that it was in the best
  interests of the community to put this matter behind us.

7.  Public Comment  This was the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on
  items not listed in any other place on the agenda. Mayor Kendrick called for
  public comment.

  George May, La Verne Library Manager, thanked City Manager Russi for
  assisting the Friends of La Verne Library in recruiting new board members and
  officers. In addition, he reported on La Verne Library events for the month of
  March.

  Joyce Kelly, 7235 Monterey, La Verne; spoke about the July, 2018, Council
  Meeting when the Council voted to eliminate Council medical coverage
  effective December 31, 2018. She stated that the Council Member in question
  could of applied for CORBA and that he/ she had plenty of time to get his own
  medical coverage.

  Jean Quinn, Via Del Sol, La Verne, spoke about Gilead Sciences and that it
  was very good news for La Verne to have them in the City.

  George Henderson, Old Town La Verne, gave an update on the Sierra
  La Verne Golf Course. He stated that meetings with the owner to address the
  future of the golf course have been scheduled.  He encouraged residents to
  attend meetings and to show solidarity to discourage certain tactics by the
  owner.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, March 4, 2019, Page 3

  Pam Berry, La Verne, stated she received an email regarding the Sierra
  La Verne Golf Course meeting with the owner advising residents that they
  need to RSVP before they can attend meetings.

  Rick McGueron, 2358 Trickling Creek, La Verne, stated that the City Council
  needs to be at all the Sierra La Verne Golf Course meetings with the owner.
  City Council support is needed.

  Lynn Del Torro, La Verne, also spoke about the Sierra La Verne Golf Course
  meetings with the owner and advised that the residents could only attend
  meetings that were assigned to them by email.

  Rick Bowen, Eagle Drive, La Verne, asked Mayor Kendrick about an invitation
  that was sent to him to address the coalition of Concern Citizens Group and
  will the Mayor be responding. He questioned why the December, 2018
  minutes were not posted on the City' s website yet. In addition, he asked about
  his records request for the document that overrode the July 16, 2018, vote of
  the Council to eliminate the Council Healthcare payments effective Dec 31,
  2018.  He asked when is a vote is not a vote and who can override a vote?

8.  Council Comments and  Council Member Carder reported on the Ribbon Cutting for Amethyst Healing
  Meeting/ Conference Reports  Spa on Arrow Highway. She stated it was a beautiful facility and she
  encouraged people to go. She reported on Dr. Seuss Read Across America
  Event held in March. She thanked Police Corporal Mark Gutierrez for his
  participation in reading to the students. She also reported on attending Coffee
  and Cocoa with a Cop event. She encouraged residents check the La Verne
  Police Department website for upcoming events and to make sure to stop by
  and get to know your La Verne Police Officers.

  Mayor Pro Tern Davis reported that the La Verne/ San Dimas Educational
  Foundation is raising funds for the District by holding the Ed Jones Memorial
  Golf Tournament on Friday, April 26, 2019. He also reported that he attended
  the USC Cycling Brackett Grant Prix Event on Sunday, March 3, 2019 and that
  it was a great event and there were many participants.

  Council Member Hepburn stated that when businesses open up they go all out
  on the Grand Opening by giving away gifts, etc. He encouraged residents to
  support La Verne' s local businesses by shopping La Verne and keeping our
  dollars in La Verne. He stated that La Verne is a good place to visit an d to
  shop and eat. He thanked everyone for attending and getting involved.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, March 4, 2019, Page 4

  Mayor Kendrick stated there are now 99 restaurants in La Verne.

  He also reported on the following:
  The Girls' Softball Opening Day;
  Garbis Peace Conference Rotary District 5300, Peacemaker of the Year
  Award Ceremony which the award was awarded to Mr. Ray La Hood,
  former United States Secretary of the Transportation from 2009- 2013 and
  representing Illinois 18th Congressional District in the United States House
  of Representatives from 1995- 2009;
  r  Bonita Unified School District State of the District;

  New Fly Over all the Traffic( FLOAT) Program which will be based at the
  La Verne Brackett Air field.
  Hillcrest Good Samaritan Dinner

  Upcoming La Verne Little League Opening Day on Saturday, March 9,
  2019;
  Upcoming Tax Measure Educational Forum for the consideration of a Tax
  Measure in the 2020 Election in March. Dates and times posted on the
  City' s website.

  Council Member Carder addressed the questions asked by Joyce Kelly and
  Rick Bowen during public comment regarding Council medical coverage. She
  stated that Council did vote to eliminate medical coverage for Council in July
  and it was to be effective on December 31, 2018. She reported that Council
  was contacted regarding the dilemma it would cause a council member if
  medical coverage were disrupted, so they agreed to extend the coverage until
  now. She stated eliminating council medical coverage is a good thing for the
  community.

  Closed Session  City Manager Russi reported that there was no need to meet in closed session
  at this time.

  Conference with Legal Counsel to discuss Pending Litigation
  Government Code Section 54956. 9 ( dl 111.

  La Verne Firefighters Association v. City of La Verne, Civil Action No. 2: 17- cv-
  08743-  GW( AFMx)

9  Adjournment  at 7: 21 pm.
